kuru.notes: MN 82 opens in Kuru country at Thullakoṭṭhika. MN 81 is a neighboring page match. The packet misses kurūnaṁ in the sixteen-country lists at AN 3.70, 8.42, 8.43 and 8.45. At AN 3.70 the English list is one segment earlier than the Pāli.

kusinārā.notes: MN 103:1.2 gives Pisinārā in the Pāli and Kusinārā in the translation. Both place the Buddha in the Baliharaṇa wood. MN 102 and AN 4.74–75 are neighboring page matches. The AN 3.132 hit is in the chapter recap.

kāla.notes: Cāpā addresses her husband as Kāḷa in Thig 13.3. The DPPN entry belongs to the independent Buddha paired with Upakāḷa at MN 116:6.9. The Pāli joins the two names as Kāḷūpakāḷā, and MN 116 is absent from the mention list.

kālaka.notes: DPD's wealthy man at Sāketa is the namesake of the monastery in AN 4.24. The candidate questions a reading about a monk in AN 10.87. The local Pāli at 1.1 reads kālaṅkataṁ bhikkhuṁ, a monk who had died, and Sujato names the monk Kalandaka. Neither establishes a monk named Kāḷaka. AN 10.86 is a neighboring page match.

kālakhemaka.notes: MN 122:2.2 names the Sakyan who owned the lodge at Kapilavatthu. MN 121 is set at Sāvatthī.

kālakārāma.notes: AN 4.24 opens at Kāḷaka’s monastery in Sāketa. AN 4.23 shares the cited page.

kālasilā.notes: The Jain ascetics at the Black Rock on Isigili appear at MN 14:15.2. The DPD hint gives MN 13. The SN passages are 4.23, 8.10 and 22.87. The mapped neighbors 4.22, 8.9 and 22.88 concern Samiddhi, Koṇḍañña and Assaji respectively.

kāligodhā.notes: SN 55.39 names the Sakyan woman, and AN 1.193 and Thag 16.7 name her as Bhaddiya’s mother. Ud 2.10:1.3 also identifies her as his mother, with the spelling kāḷīgodhāya. SN 55.38 and the two AN ranges flanking 1.188–197 are page matches.

kālī.notes: AN 1.267 and AN 10.26 both call the laywoman kuraragharikā. MN 21 names Vedehikā’s maid, and in MN 50 Moggallāna recalls his sister when he was Dūsī. Two verse passages are missing from the packet. Thig 5.6:6.1 attributes the nun’s verses to Mittā kāḷī therī. Thag 2.16:1.1–5 describes the woman handling the bones in Mahākāḷa’s verse. Sujato renders kāḷī there as ‘black’. The episode identifies the woman in Kāḷī 05. The AN ranges flanking 1.258–267 are page matches.

kāmabhū.notes: SN 35.233 names Ānanda’s interlocutor at Kosambī. Citta’s two conversations with Kāmabhū are SN 41.5 and 41.6. The mapped SN 35.232 and 41.4 feature other monks. SN 35.237 and 41.10 mention Kāmabhū in chapter recaps.

kāmada.notes: Kāmada speaks in SN 2.6. The other mapped discourses name their speakers as Dāmali (2.5), Pañcālacaṇḍa (2.7) and Tāyana (2.8).

kāmaṇḍā.notes: SN 35.133 places Udāyī at Kāmaṇḍā in Todeyya’s mango grove. The adjacent SN 35.132 takes place at Makkarakata in Avanti.

kāraṇapālī.notes: Kāraṇapālī questions Piṅgiyānī in AN 5.194. AN 5.193 features Saṅgārava, and AN 5.200:7.2 lists discourse titles in the chapter recap.

kāsi.notes: DN 19:36.9 distinguishes Bārāṇasī from the Kāsis whose capital it is. MN 26:25.19 calls the destination kāsinaṁ puraṁ, ‘the city of the Kāsis’, and 26.1 names it Bārāṇasī. DPPN only tentatively equates Bārāṇasī with Phussa’s birthplace in Kāsi 02. The packet misses the kingdom in the sixteen-country lists at AN 3.70, 8.42, 8.43 and 8.45. AN 10.28 is a page match for 10.29. At Thig 12.1:9.3, mā kāsi is a verb, ‘do not do’.

kātiyāna.notes: Thag 6.7 gives the elder’s verses. SN 2.30:8.1 names the sectarian teacher Pakudhaka Kātiyāna. The packet offers no entry for him.

kātiyānī.notes: AN 1.265 singles out Kātiyānī for her confidence. The ranges 1.248–257 and 1.268–277 share the cited page.

kūṭāgārasālā.notes: The packet reports zero mentions. AN 8.53:1.1 and MN 36:1.2 both give vesāliyaṁ … mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ. Sujato translates the name as ‘the hall with the peaked roof’. Many page matches concern other settings, including Kapilavatthu in AN 3.73, Ukkacelā in MN 34, Elephant Village in SN 35.125, and Sāvatthī in SN 55.28–29.

lakkhaṇa.notes: SN 19.1:1.3 explicitly places Venerable Lakkhaṇa on Gijjhakūṭa with Mahāmoggallāna. Sujato translates his name as ‘Mark’, so the packet misses him. The adjacent SN 18.22 concerns Rāhula.

lohicca.notes: DPD cites DN 12, where Lohicca lives at Sālavatikā and sends his barber to invite the Buddha. In SN 35.132 his students visit Mahākaccāna’s hut at Makkarakata. SN 35.133:8.4 lists the preceding Lohicca discourse in the chapter recap. Its own story concerns Udāyī and the brahmin lady of the Verahaccāni clan.

macchikāsaṇḍa.notes: DPD glosses Macchikāsaṇḍa as a forest. Its own example, SN 41.4:1.1, distinguishes the locality Macchikāsaṇḍa from the grove Ambāṭakavana where the monks stayed. DPPN calls the locality a township. SN 40.11 shares the page with SN 41.1.

maddakucchi.notes: SN 1.38 and 4.13 open in the Maddakucchi deer park. SN 1.37 and 4.12 have other settings. DN 16:3.42.9 recalls the Buddha’s hint to Ānanda at the park. The encounter with Māra described in the entry is in SN 4.13.
